clue.text: Refined female visiting Channel Islands and California

indicators.note: a guest visiting stays inside the house, so the female goes within the other letters

parts.note: a lass is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A cultured woman tours Jersey, Guernsey and the American West Coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands are the British islands off Normandy, Jersey and Guernsey the largest.
explanation.definitionFit: Classical taste is restrained and elegant, a synonym for refined in style.

clue.text: Allowing church bell's noise?

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England
ding is the sound a struck bell makes

explanation.surface: Is a church's ringing permitted, the clue asks.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceding means yielding or granting, so it works as a synonym for allowing or conceding.

clue.text: Shrewd like trustee, every now and then

parts.note: as means like, in the sense of 'such as'

indicators.note: taking letters only now and then means keeping every other letter of trustee

explanation.surface: Someone is described as occasionally canny, like a trustee should be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like' looks like part of the description but gives AS; 'every now and then' keeps the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of trustee, TUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute and shrewd are close synonyms for sharp practical judgement.

clue.text: Sister hides cards inside very big hats

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it within you, so the sister's letters wrap the card game

parts.note: SR is the abbreviation for Sister, as in a nun's title
ombre is an old Spanish card game
OS stands for outsize, the clothing size for very large

explanation.surface: A nun conceals playing cards under some enormous headwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Ombre was a fashionable three-player card game in the 17th and 18th centuries.
explanation.definitionFit: Sombreros are broad-brimmed Mexican hats, so the plural noun is an example of hats.

clue.text: Flying Fortresses just daydreams?

definitions.meaning: read literally, fortresses that are flying are strongholds up in the sky
an idiom for impractical fantasies or schemes that will never come true

explanation.surface: Were the wartime American bombers nothing more than fantasies?
explanation.walkthrough: The Flying Fortress was the B-17 bomber; capital letters hide the plain reading of airborne forts.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names visionary plans with no foundation, exactly what daydreams are.

clue.text: Famous Italian diva can do role in broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, as seed is sown, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A celebrated Italian opera star can perform a part on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges all fifteen letters of 'diva can do role in'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Renaissance painter of the Mona Lisa is surely the best-known Italian of all.

clue.text: State out loud what could be affected by 23

indicators.note: spoken out loud, the word for state is heard rather than seen

parts.note: to cite is to state or quote

explanation.surface: Say aloud what might suffer from the condition in another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is EYESTRAIN, which can impair one's vision.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision is the faculty that tired, strained eyes can weaken.

clue.text: Extremely stylish twelve inch dress

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, here of stylish

parts.note: twelve inches make one foot: I for one and FT for foot

explanation.surface: A very fashionable twelve-inch frock, a mini indeed.
explanation.definitionFit: A shift is a simple straight dress hanging from the shoulders.

clue.text: Great music show with singer Adam in charge

parts.note: a gig is a live performance of music
Adam Ant was a British pop singer of the early 1980s

explanation.surface: A fine concert featuring Adam, who is in charge of proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam Ant fronted Adam and the Ants, a big British New Romantic act.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigantic means huge, matching great in its sense of very large.

clue.text: Part of boat's equipment seen as pilot's turned

indicators.note: turned means twisted round into another shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some boat gear is seen as belonging to the pilot, who has changed course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' rearranges AS and PILOTS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Topsails are sails set above the lowest sail on a mast, part of a sailing ship's rig.

clue.text: Digest antidepressants initially, then stomach a bit of dope

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: tum is an informal word for the stomach

explanation.surface: Swallow some pills first, then keep down a little cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' looks like drugs, but here it is slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for information, and a datum is a single item of information.

clue.text: Making an appearance is embarrassing

definitions.meaning: to make someone look bad or put them to shame in front of others

explanation.surface: Turning up is a mortifying experience.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to arrive and to humiliate someone by comparison.

clue.text: Talented actor, perhaps, not wearing make-up?

definitions.meaning: someone with inborn ability, a gifted performer being one example
unadorned, as a face shown without cosmetics

explanation.surface: A gifted performer appears bare-faced on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person with innate talent and an unmade-up, unaffected look.

clue.text: Newly-formed nation led by a woman

indicators.note: something led by another comes before it, so the rearranged letters precede the a
the nation is formed anew, so its letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A new country headed by a female leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonia is a female first name, so the bearer is an example of a woman.

clue.text: Democrat absorbed by awful peril in East, as Roosevelt was

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase describing the holder of the top office

indicators.note: something absorbed is taken in, so the Democrat goes inside the jumbled letters
awful suggests something badly made, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics

explanation.surface: A Democrat faces terrible danger in the East, as Roosevelt did in wartime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges PERIL IN EAST; 'absorbed by' puts D inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Franklin and Theodore Roosevelt were both US presidents, hence of presidential rank.

clue.text: Ferns originally and now trees spreading … here?

definitions.text: Ferns originally and now trees spreading … here?

indicators.note: spreading means sprawling out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
originally means at the start, picking the first letter of Ferns

explanation.surface: A place where bracken came first and woodland now spreads out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreading' rearranges F (from 'Ferns originally') with NOW TREES. The New Forest is a large ancient woodland and heath in Hampshire, southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue pictures this English woodland, full of bracken and trees.

clue.text: John briefly in a bit of a depression? That's touching

indicators.note: the shortened name sits inside the hollow

parts.note: a dent is a small hollow pressed into a surface

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: Jack is a familiar form of the name John

explanation.surface: Johnny is feeling a little low, which is rather moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' suggests low mood but means a hollow. 'briefly' cuts JACK to JAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjacent things border or abut each other, so they are touching.

clue.text: Dine with fellow, hosted by crazy screwball?

indicators.note: a guest hosted by someone is inside their home, so these letters go within the crazy word

parts.note: mad means crazy
to dine is to eat
he stands for a man or fellow

explanation.surface: Having supper with a man at the home of a lunatic eccentric.
explanation.definitionFit: A meathead is a stupid person, and screwball is slang for an oddball or fool.

clue.text: Carpeting and gauze reduced in price

parts.note: a dressing is a covering for a wound, often gauze
prices that are down have been cut

explanation.surface: Floor covering and bandage material sold off cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpeting' looks like floor coverings but means a scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is to rebuke them, so carpeting is a severe reprimand.

clue.text: Successfully handling piece of masonry

definitions.meaning: managing well in a difficult situation
the top course of a wall, usually sloping to shed rain

explanation.surface: A builder dealing well with some stonework.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both managing a situation and the capping layer on top of a wall.

clue.text: Leave pudding son heartily rejected

indicators.note: the son is thrown out from the heart of the word for pudding

parts.note: pudding is British for dessert, the sweet course

explanation.surface: A boy wholeheartedly refuses his sweet course and leaves the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartily rejected' takes out the middle S of DESSERT.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert is to abandon or leave someone or something.

clue.text: One who's against old church in Turkish city

parts.note: an anti is an opponent of something

explanation.surface: A dissenter from the old church lives in a city in Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: Antioch, now Antakya, was an early centre of Christianity.
explanation.definitionFit: Antioch is an ancient city in southern Turkey, an example of a Turkish city.

clue.text: External device on computer with top missing

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is dropped

parts.note: a router is a device that links a computer to a network

explanation.surface: A piece of computer hardware lacks its cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Outer means on the outside, a synonym for external.

clue.text: New novel about one old music maker

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the other two
new means made afresh, so the letters of novel are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fresh story about a single antique instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges NOVEL into V-LONE, and 'about' puts I and O inside after the V.
explanation.definitionFit: The violone is a large bass viol, an instrument and so a maker of music.

clue.text: Problem for reader — that's right — in English school

indicators.note: the affirmative is placed inside the other letters

parts.note: to school someone is to train them
yes is said to confirm something is right

explanation.surface: A pupil at an English school struggles with reading, and that is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' looks like a noun but is the verb, to train.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired eyes from long reading are a common complaint for anyone who reads a lot.

clue.text: Ban last of the X-Files (middle section only)

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, here of the
keeping only the middle section drops the first and last letters of Files

explanation.surface: Bin the final episodes of the sci-fi TV series, keeping just the middle ones.
explanation.walkthrough: The X-Files was a 1990s American TV series about the paranormal.
explanation.definitionFit: To exile someone is to banish them, so it is a synonym for ban.

clue.text: House outwardly unfinished in rocky place

indicators.note: the outside letters are placed within the rocky hill

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

indicators.note: outwardly means showing only the outside, the first and last letters of unfinished

explanation.surface: A half-built home perched on a craggy hilltop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' is a royal dynasty here, not a dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the English royal house of Henry VIII and Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Waterproof is not suitable when going outside

indicators.note: the suitable word goes around the outside of the colloquial is not

parts.note: right means suitable or fitting
ain't is a colloquial contraction of is not

explanation.surface: A coat isn't fit to wear outdoors in the wet.
explanation.walkthrough: AINT is the slang 'ain't', apostrophe dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Raintight means keeping rain out, which a waterproof thing does.
